lines.text: Did you know that the United States Mint loses tens of millions of dollars every single year making pennies?
Due to soaring raw metal prices, a one-cent coin currently costs three point zero seven cents to produce.
Pennies haven't been solid copper since nineteen eighty-two; they are ninety-seven point five percent zinc with a thin copper plating.
So why does the government keep minting billions of unprofitable coins?
The answer is zinc industry lobbying, charity donation drives, and public fear of retail price rounding.
Countries like Canada and Australia abolished their one-cent coins years ago with huge financial savings.
Would you support the United States finally retiring the penny for good?
